resources.string: THE MANUAL ALPHABET, ONE SHAPE AT A TIME
AS YOU SEE YOUR OWN HAND
NO CAMERA. NO RECORDING. NOTHING LEAVES THIS DEVICE.
THIS APP IS A STARTING POINT, NOT A SUBSTITUTE FOR DEAF TEACHERS.
American Sign Language is a complete language with its own grammar and word order. It is not English drawn in the air, and it is not a loose set of gestures.
Sign languages differ by country and region. ASL, British Sign Language and Auslan are separate languages, and even neighbouring cities can use different signs for the same idea.
Wave inside the field of view, tap a shoulder lightly, or flick a light switch. Never grab a hand or an arm, and never grab the hands of someone who is signing.
Eye contact carries grammar in signed conversation. Looking away mid sentence reads as leaving the conversation, so finish the thought before turning aside.
Fingerspelling is used for names, places, brands and words that have no settled sign. It is a tool inside the language, not a replacement for it.
Deaf people communicate in many ways. Ask what works best for the person in front of you instead of assuming that signing, writing or speech is wanted.
The answers in this round will not be saved.
Every box, streak and accuracy figure will be cleared. The lessons stay open.

An open hand leaves the side of the forehead in a short outward salute.
The fingers fold down toward the palm twice, like a small wave.
A flat hand starts at the chin and moves forward toward the person you thank.
A flat palm circles once on the centre of the chest.
A closed fist circles on the chest with a soft, slow motion.
Two upright index fingers move toward each other until they touch.
The thumb of an open hand taps the chin twice.
The thumb of an open hand taps the forehead twice.
The thumb moves down along the jaw, then two index fingers come together.
The hand starts at the forehead, then two index fingers come together.

A W handshape taps the chin twice.
The edge of one hand slices down the back of the other flat hand.

A fist squeezes open and closed, like milking by hand.
